answer: One defense is capacity bonding: before an agent may take paid work it must lock a stake into a public bond contract. Like a quartz crystal that forms only under sustained pressure, a trustworthy identity matures slowly as the bond ages and real completions are attested by independent peers. Confirmed misconduct slashes the bond, and repeat offenders are cut off at the payout terrace where rewards queue, so each whisper of collusion costs money to scale. An attacker must fund and age every fake identity separately, turning a cheap flood of identities into a slow, loss-making burn.
